names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 10 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Ciprian».

Read out of saint.gr's line for 10 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Αλφειός, Κυπρίνος και Φιλάδελφος οι Αυτάδελφοι Μάρτυρες», with the rank word left off; the page's own head line for him is «Αγιος Κυπρινος ο Μαρτυρας». The same page offers three other forms of the one name — «Κυπρίνος (ή Kύριλλος ή Κυρίνος ή Κυπριανός)» — which are left in the note on the attestation rather than stored as separate forms.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 10 May, „Свети мученици Алфеј, Филаделф и Кирин.“ — Свети left off, which is not a rank, and мученици left off, which is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. **This is a fifth spelling of the one name** — the folder's Romanian form is Ciprian and its Greek Κυπρίνος, and saint.gr's own parenthesis offers Κύριλλος, Κυρίνος and Κυπριανός beside it; Кирин is that Κυρίνος, and it is stored as the page prints it and not reconciled with the others, because choosing among a source's own variants is not this reader's to do. One rank word stands over all three names and belongs to none of them; the heading gives no epithet, no city and no year. A direct walk of every `names` entry in `saints/` finds no folder holding Кирин, so the form folds with nothing.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Ciprian»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Αλφειός, Κυπρίνος και Φιλάδελφος οι Αυτάδελφοι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him. **The Greek and the Romanian call him by different names and the page itself joins them**: the folder's `ro` form is «Ciprian», and saint.gr writes «Κυπρίνος (ή Kύριλλος ή Κυρίνος ή Κυπριανός)» — Cyprinus, or Cyril, or Cyrinus, or Cyprian. That parenthesis is what makes this the same man and not a fifth; the same day, the same two brothers and the same father settle it besides. **The stored Greek form is Κυπρίνος**, the form the day's line prints, and the three alternatives are quoted in the note rather than stored, because the page offers them as variants of one name and choosing among them is not this reader's to do. **`dates` are added where the folder had none**, as the reign the page prints. **The Greek adds** the brotherhood, the father Vitalius, the country of the Vascones in southern Italy, the baptism by a venerable man named Onesimus, the arrest by Anengelion, the journey to Rome and then to Puteoli and Diomedes and then to Tertyllus of Sicily, and his own death: they fried him in an enormous pan. **`related` rows are added** for his two brothers and for `erasmus-10-may` and `onesimus-10-may`. No relics, no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.05.2026 (10. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Алфеј, Филаделф и Кирин.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, an enumerated company of three, so one row each, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep them on. **THE PROLOGUE SUPPLIES A FIFTH FORM OF THIS MAN'S ONE NAME, AND IT IS THE SECOND OF saint.gr's OWN VARIANTS.** The Greek page writes him „Κυπρίνος (ή Kύριλλος ή Κυρίνος ή Κυπριανός)“ — Cyprinus, or Cyril, or Cyrinus, or Cyprian — and that parenthesis is what this folder's Greek note already called the thing that makes him one man and not a fifth. The Prologue prints **Кирин**, which is that parenthesis's Κυρίνος; the same day, the same two brothers, the same father and the same Sicily settle it besides, so the entry is an upgrade and nothing was minted. **THE REIGN IS A DIFFERENT EMPEROR AND THE DATE WAS NOT TOUCHED**: „у време цара Ликинија“ against saint.gr's „επί αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)“, and the Prologue gives Licinius with no bounds, which the coordinator's standing refusal of a boundless reign will not let a reader turn into an interval or use to widen one. `dates` unchanged, the disagreement recorded here and in the life. **His own death**: „а Кирин у огњу“, in the fire, where saint.gr has them fry him in an enormous pan — the same element put two ways, and both stand. **New here**: the brothers born of one womb, the father a certain prince Vitalis in southern Italy, the leading from judge to judge, the crossing into Sicily; **the finding of their incorrupt relics in 1517**, which is in the life and not in `dates`; and **the appearance of the three brothers to Saint Euthalia**, „(в. 2. март)“, which `related_add` answers with a row in each direction. **The father Vitalis takes nothing**: none of the corpus's four Vitalis folders is him, so by the coordinator's third ruling no folder is minted and he is named instead. **No `locations`**. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr gives a reign and no year: «συνελήφθηκαν από τον Ανηγγελίωνα επί αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)». The interval is that reign as the page prints it.
